properties.name: MEASURED 2026-09-22: edges do NOT widen search_design at all, and the tool that DOES use them has its shared-neighbour signal swamped by the author edge — 4 of 5 candidates were offered because "both relate to who:claude-code"
properties.statement:
ANTHONY ASKED, 2026-09-22: when related topics are found, are they linked so that FUTURE SEARCHES pull the primary and the related together? Measured rather than assumed, and the answer has three parts.

═══ ① AN EDGE DOES NOTHING FOR `search_design`. MEASURED. ═══

`dec:idea-lifecycle-dimensions-on-a-requirement` was linked ANTICIPATES to `dec:idea-what-drives-a-capability-up-the-ladder...` earlier the same day. Searching text unique to the second returned it at 32.9 and the linked node DID NOT APPEAR IN THE TOP EIGHT AT ALL. `search_design` is BM25 over each node's own name/statement/description; it does not traverse edges and never has. **Drawing a relation does not improve recall on the tool people search with.**

⇒ SO THE MENTAL MODEL "link it and future searches will find both" IS FALSE, and it is worth saying plainly because it is the natural assumption and it changes what linking is FOR.

═══ ② WHERE EDGES DO COMPOUND ═══

`relation_candidates` genuinely walks them: its `because` names "a shared neighbour — two nodes that both relate to a third are related in the graph's own terms, whatever their words". Observed working in this very call: one candidate was offered because "both relate to fact:every-link-of-the-founding-chain…", an edge drawn an hour earlier. `topic_report` also reads each hit's connections, and `propagate_change` is edges end to end. So linking pays off in the LINKING and PROPAGATION tools, and not in search.

═══ 🛑 ③ AND THE SHARED-NEIGHBOUR SIGNAL IS CURRENTLY SWAMPED BY AUTHORSHIP ═══

Of five candidates returned for one node, FOUR cited the same reason: **"both relate to who:claude-code"**. That is an AUTHORED_BY edge to a Contributor that nearly every recent node carries. It is a hub, and sharing a hub is not evidence of relatedness — every node this agent has ever written "relates to" it.

⭐ THE TOOL RARITY-WEIGHTS ITS TERMS AND NOT ITS NEIGHBOURS. Its own description says distinctive terms are "weighted by rarity ACROSS THE POOL, so words true of everything count for nothing" — exactly the right treatment, applied to the text half only. The neighbour half has no such discount, so one Contributor with hundreds of edges outranks a genuinely distinctive shared subject.

⚠️ AND THE DESIGN ALREADY KNEW THIS, FROM THE MEASUREMENT THAT CREATED THE LINKING DISCIPLINE. 2026-08-21: "reflow2's own graph held 145 brainstormed ideas joined by 12 edges; 111 of them reached no other idea within two hops, and THE MOST COMMON EDGE ON AN IDEA WAS ITS AUTHOR." The candidate ranker was then built on shared neighbours without discounting that exact hub, so it inherited the very skew the measurement had already named.

═══ AND THE COVERAGE IS THIN ANYWAY ═══

`relation_coverage(Decision, DEPENDS_ON, outgoing)`: **133 of 773 live Decisions — 17%.** One edge type of thirteen, so it is indicative rather than total, but the shape matches the 2026-08-21 reading: most ideas still reach nothing.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether discounting hub neighbours by degree would leave enough signal to rank on, or whether the text half is carrying the tool already. That is a one-query experiment against the existing pool and has not been run.



RE-MEASURED 2026-10-07, still true, and nothing has changed it since: relation_candidates on req:one-search-reaches-every-design-a-hub-tracks gave "both relate to who:ajs" as the first reason for its top candidates, and 1 of its top 10 was in the subject's actual family (0 of 10 for req:recursive-black-box-decomposition). Its pool is the subject's own node type unless pool_type is passed. See fact:root-cause-idea-linking-covers-open-ideas-in-pairs-and-a-vision-spread-across-requirements-is-never-gathered-2026-10-07.
